name: Ominous Core 24 standalone presentation prototype
status: inspectable candidate; browser-unverified; not integrated or published
checked: Explicit field projection and strict public schema
Host state clearing and isolated controller logic
Synthetic leak detection, including deliberately injected failure
Input consumption limited to 65537 bytes; regular files only
Approval descriptor snapshot and malicious array cases
Non-overwrite output and separate digest receipt
not_verified: Installed Ominous GPT or any other core/product
browser_note: 10 scenarios intentionally not run because the environment browser/IPC route was restricted. No blocked launch, loopback retry, escalation or security-setting change occurred.

independent_review.important_fixes: Both fixed by author with failing regression tests followed by full green tests in commit f46ed85615e287cae5cdfe3118d113656b09d8de.
independent_review.deferred_minor: An invalid browser-controller state keeps an already-approved title while the host API clears it. Both show error and clear result text. The fake-DOM parity test normalizes the invalid state and does not compare title; normal UI choices are valid states.

decisions: New isolated source repository; no existing core sources or allocations changed
No product connection, public hosting, new permission or deployment
Fixed controller tested in a minimal fake DOM; these are logic checks, not browser acceptance
Branch retained locally; no merge, push or pull request
limitations: Approval is an explicit caller-controlled data boundary, not a secret detector. Text put in an approved field is disclosed.
HTML contains ordinary public UI JavaScript; this is not source-code access control or an unmonitorability claim.
Diagnostic folder separation is not authentication or an OS access-control guarantee.
